  // Restore the saved color scheme preference, or
  // enact the browser preference if "automatic", 
  // without expecting DOM load to have completed.
  //
  // Also restore any saved readingmode and ToC display preferences.
  function initializeReadingPreferences() {
    let saved_theme = localStorage.getItem("ar5iv_theme") || "automatic";
    if (saved_theme === "automatic") {
      if (window.matchMedia("(prefers-color-scheme: dark)").matches) {
        saved_theme = "dark";
      }
    }
    if (saved_theme == "dark") {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-theme", "dark");
    } else {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-theme", "light");
    }

    const tocDisplay = localStorage.getItem('arxiv_html_paper_toc_display');
    if (tocDisplay) {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-toc-display", tocDisplay);
    }
    const readingMode = localStorage.getItem('arxiv_html_paper_reading_mode');
    if (readingMode) {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-reading-mode", readingMode);
    }
    // Pre-apply spinout-banner dismissal here, before the banner paints, so it
    // never flashes in only to be hidden later by the deferred arxiv-header.js.
    // Key matches arxiv-header.js: "arxiv-banner-dismissed:" + data-banner-name.
    if (localStorage.getItem('arxiv-banner-dismissed:spinout-nonprofit')) {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-banner-dismissed", "");
    }
  }
  // Run as soon as JS starts, to minimize repainting
  initializeReadingPreferences();
</script>

<li class="ltx_tocentry ltx_tocentry_subsection"><a href="#S4.SS3" title="In IV Experiments ‣ CoRe-WM: Conditioned Response-State World Modeling for Longitudinal Treatment-Response Prediction in Breast DCE-MRI" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_title"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_ref"><span class="ltx_text">IV-C</span> </span><span class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Comparison with Other Methods</span></span></a>
<ol class="ltx_toclist ltx_toclist_subsection">

</ol></li>
<li class="ltx_tocentry ltx_tocentry_subsection"><a href="#S4.SS4" title="In IV Experiments ‣ CoRe-WM: Conditioned Response-State World Modeling for Longitudinal Treatment-Response Prediction in Breast DCE-MRI" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_title"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_ref"><span class="ltx_text">IV-D</span> </span><span class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Cross-Cohort Transfer to I-SPY1</span></span></a></li>

<article class="ltx_document ltx_authors_1line">
<h1 class="ltx_title ltx_title_document"><span id="id1" class="ltx_text">CoRe-WM</span>: Conditioned Response-State World Modeling for Longitudinal Treatment-Response Prediction in Breast DCE-MRI</h1>
<div class="ltx_authors">

USA.</span></span></span><span id="id7" class="ltx_note ltx_note_frontmatter ltx_thanks_correspondence ltx_role_thanks"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">†</sup><span class="ltx_note_outer"><span class="ltx_note_content"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">†</sup><span class="ltx_note_type">thanks: </span>Corresponding authors: Lin Zhao (lin.zhao.1@njit.edu) and Tianming Liu (tliu@uga.edu).</span></span></span></span></div>

<div id="abstract1" class="ltx_abstract"><h6 class="ltx_title ltx_title_abstract">Abstract</h6>
    
<p id="abstract1.1" class="ltx_p">Pathologic complete response (pCR) after neoadjuvant chemotherapy is a key prognostic indicator in aggressive breast cancer, yet existing prediction approaches either rely on pretreatment imaging alone, missing the patient’s evolving response, or optimize multi-visit classifiers under direct outcome supervision, coupling representation learning with the clinical endpoint. We formulate longitudinal pCR prediction as a world-modeling problem and propose Conditioned Response-state World Modeling (<span id="abstract1.1.1" class="ltx_text">CoRe-WM</span>), which learns a latent state-transition model that predicts the next imaging state from the observed sequence. The transition function is conditioned on patient clinical profile and assigned therapy through additive shift and feature-wise modulation, enabling patient- and treatment-specific dynamics. A Factorized Response State pathway further decouples treatment-response dynamics from imaging appearance by encoding the structural prior that response manifests primarily in lesion morphology. After pretraining, all parameters are frozen and a linear readout predicts pCR at each clinical decision point. We evaluate <span id="abstract1.1.2" class="ltx_text">CoRe-WM</span> on I-SPY2 under five-fold cross-validation and assess cross-cohort transfer on I-SPY1. <span id="abstract1.1.3" class="ltx_text">CoRe-WM</span> achieves the highest discrimination among all evaluated methods at every prospective decision point, and demonstrates robust cross-cohort transfer. Ablation studies identify patient-profile conditioning and the factorized response pathway as the principal contributors. These results establish world-model-based representation learning as a promising framework for outcome prediction in oncology and beyond.</p>
  
</div>
<div class="ltx_keywords">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_title_keywords">Index Terms: </h6>Breast cancer, dynamic contrast-enhanced MRI, joint-embedding predictive
architecture, longitudinal imaging, neoadjuvant therapy, pathologic complete
response, world model.

</div>
<section id="S1" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">I </span><span id="S1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Introduction</span></h2>

<div id="S1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Pathologic complete response (pCR), conventionally determined by pathological examination of post-treatment tissue, is strongly associated with favorable long-term outcomes, particularly in aggressive breast cancer subtypes <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib1" title="" class="ltx_ref">1</a>, <a href="#bib.bib2" title="" class="ltx_ref">2</a>, <a href="#bib.bib3" title="" class="ltx_ref">3</a>]</cite>. Pretreatment prediction of pCR could indicate whether a patient is likely to respond to the planned regimen. Extending such prediction across multiple candidate regimens would further enable estimating and comparing expected response to each option, supporting individualized treatment selection.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Recent studies have investigated pCR prediction in breast cancer using dynamic contrast-enhanced (DCE) MRI, which characterizes contrast-enhancement kinetics related to tumor perfusion, vascular permeability, and angiogenic activity. Early approaches extracted response-related patterns from pretreatment imaging alone <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib4" title="" class="ltx_ref">4</a>, <a href="#bib.bib5" title="" class="ltx_ref">5</a>, <a href="#bib.bib6" title="" class="ltx_ref">6</a>, <a href="#bib.bib7" title="" class="ltx_ref">7</a>]</cite>. Ha <em id="S1.p2.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">et al.</em> applied a pretrained CNN to pretreatment postcontrast MRI to predict treatment response <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib8" title="" class="ltx_ref">8</a>]</cite>, while Braman <em id="S1.p2.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">et al.</em> modeled intratumoral and peritumoral DCE-MRI features with multi-institutional validation in patients receiving HER2-targeted therapy <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib9" title="" class="ltx_ref">9</a>]</cite>. Subsequent work incorporated richer imaging representations and non-imaging variables. Peng <em id="S1.p2.1.3" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">et al.</em> showed that deep features from pretreatment DCE-MRI provided stronger pCR discrimination than radiomics <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib10" title="" class="ltx_ref">10</a>]</cite>, and Duanmu <em id="S1.p2.1.4" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">et al.</em> integrated MRI with molecular and demographic variables to complement baseline imaging <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib11" title="" class="ltx_ref">11</a>]</cite>. Notably, pCR rates vary substantially with patient profiles, including receptor subtype, exceeding 40% in HER2-positive and triple-negative tumors while remaining below 20% in HR-positive/HER2-negative disease <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib1" title="" class="ltx_ref">1</a>, <a href="#bib.bib12" title="" class="ltx_ref">12</a>, <a href="#bib.bib13" title="" class="ltx_ref">13</a>]</cite>. Receptor status, genomic risk, and other clinical characteristics therefore constitute strong baseline prognostic factors whose interaction with the administered therapy shapes individual treatment response. Across existing imaging methods, these clinical and treatment variables are either omitted or appended as covariates in the outcome classifier rather than integrated into the modeling of treatment response, limiting the capacity to represent patient-specific response patterns.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Beyond this representational gap, these pretreatment approaches cannot incorporate the patient’s evolving response once treatment begins or update predictions as new imaging evidence becomes available. As treatment proceeds, serial DCE-MRI examinations reveal patient-specific changes in tumor size, morphology, and enhancement that reflect the ongoing treatment effect <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib5" title="" class="ltx_ref">5</a>]</cite>. These on-treatment observations motivate longitudinal approaches that update the pCR estimate as new examinations become available. Several studies have explored this setting. Jing <em id="S1.p3.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">et al.</em> used DCE-MRI acquired at multiple treatment timepoints for pCR prediction <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib14" title="" class="ltx_ref">14</a>]</cite>, Gao <em id="S1.p3.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">et al.</em> combined longitudinal imaging with multimodal clinical information <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib15" title="" class="ltx_ref">15</a>]</cite>, and Tang <em id="S1.p3.1.3" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">et al.</em> modeled spatiotemporal interactions between baseline and early-treatment MRI <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib16" title="" class="ltx_ref">16</a>]</cite>. Together, these studies demonstrated that on-treatment imaging provides additional predictive information beyond the pretreatment examination. However, existing longitudinal approaches generally optimize a multi-visit classifier under direct pCR supervision rather than model the dynamics of treatment response. The temporal evolution of tumor state, characterized by the rate, timing, and pattern of morphological change under therapy, carries predictive information distinct from any single-visit or fixed-pair snapshot. Capturing these dynamics requires a model that represents treatment response as an evolving state trajectory and progressively refines its prediction as each new examination arrives.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p4.1" class="ltx_p">Motivated by this need, we formulate longitudinal pCR prediction as a world-modeling problem. A world model learns to predict future states from the current state and an applied action, building an internal representation of the underlying dynamics rather than mapping observations directly to outcomes <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib17" title="" class="ltx_ref">17</a>, <a href="#bib.bib18" title="" class="ltx_ref">18</a>, <a href="#bib.bib19" title="" class="ltx_ref">19</a>, <a href="#bib.bib20" title="" class="ltx_ref">20</a>, <a href="#bib.bib21" title="" class="ltx_ref">21</a>]</cite>. The world we are modeling is patients’ treatment response. As therapy is administered, the lesion evolves, and serial DCE-MRI examinations capture successive snapshots of this evolution. In this formulation, each MRI observation defines the patient state, and the assigned therapy together with individual clinical profiles (e.g., receptor status, age) serve as the condition that governs patient-specific evolution. A learned transition function takes the observed state sequence and this condition to predict the latent representation of the next visit, progressively refining its representation of the treatment response dynamics as each new observation arrives. We instantiate this formulation within the Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture (JEPA) <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib20" title="" class="ltx_ref">20</a>, <a href="#bib.bib21" title="" class="ltx_ref">21</a>]</cite> as Conditioned Response-state World Modeling (<span id="S1.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text">CoRe-WM</span>). A conditioned causal Transformer forms the transition core, with treatment and clinical information entering through additive shift and feature-wise modulation to shape the dynamics. Because treatment response manifests most directly in changes in lesion volume, shape, and morphology, a parallel Factorized Response State (<span id="S1.p4.1.2" class="ltx_text">FRS</span>) pathway encodes this structural prior by operating on compact geometry descriptors, guiding the learned representation toward treatment-relevant changes. Image-derived Response Guidance (<span id="S1.p4.1.3" class="ltx_text">IRG</span>) reinforces this pathway through supervision derived from inter-visit morphological and enhancement changes. After pretraining, all parameters are frozen and a Frozen Linear Readout (<span id="S1.p4.1.4" class="ltx_text">FLR</span>) maps the accumulated response states to pCR prediction at each decision point. We pretrain and evaluate <span id="S1.p4.1.5" class="ltx_text">CoRe-WM</span> on 808 I-SPY2 patients <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib13" title="" class="ltx_ref">13</a>]</cite> with four-visit DCE-MRI under five-fold cross-validation, and assess cross-cohort transfer on 156 I-SPY1 patients <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib22" title="" class="ltx_ref">22</a>]</cite>. <span id="S1.p4.1.6" class="ltx_text">CoRe-WM</span> achieves the highest AUROC among all evaluated methods at every prospective decision point, outperforming matched supervised baselines and reproduced longitudinal approaches on I-SPY2, and demonstrates competitive cross-cohort transfer to I-SPY1.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p5.1" class="ltx_p">Our contributions are as follows:</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p6" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p6.1" class="ltx_p">a) We formulate longitudinal treatment-response prediction as a world-modeling problem: instead of training a multi-visit classifier that maps imaging directly to pCR, the model learns a state-transition function that predicts the next latent patient state given the current state, assigned therapy, and patient clinical profiles. This world-model formulation shifts the learning objective from outcome classification to modeling treatment-response dynamics, enabling progressive risk updating as new examinations arrive.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p7" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p7.1" class="ltx_p">b) We introduce a Factorized Response State that decouples treatment-response dynamics from high-dimensional imaging appearance via a compact parallel pathway operating on lesion geometry descriptors. This factorization encodes an explicit structural prior that treatment response manifests primarily in lesion morphology, reducing the representational burden on the world model and its dependence on large training sets.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p8" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p8.1" class="ltx_p">c) We integrate clinical/treatment conditioning directly into the state-transition function through dual mechanisms (additive shift and feature-wise modulation), so that treatment and patient clinical profiles shape the learned response trajectory rather than entering only at classification time. The condition-permutation analysis confirms that this conditioning is encoded in the frozen response state itself.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p9" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p9.1" class="ltx_p">d) We evaluate on I-SPY2 under five-fold cross-validation and on I-SPY1 for cross-cohort transfer. <span id="S1.p9.1.1" class="ltx_text">CoRe-WM</span> achieves the highest AUROC at every prospective decision point on I-SPY2 and demonstrates cross-cohort robustness on I-SPY1, providing a novel pathway toward world-model-based longitudinal treatment-response prediction.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S2" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">II </span><span id="S2.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Related Work</span></h2>

<section id="S2.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection"><span id="S2.SS1.6" class="ltx_text">II-A</span> </span><span id="S2.SS1.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Breast DCE-MRI and pCR Prediction</span></h3>

<div id="S2.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Quantitative DCE-MRI established that longitudinal changes in functional tumor volume are associated with pathologic response and recurrence-free survival in the I-SPY trials <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib4" title="" class="ltx_ref">4</a>, <a href="#bib.bib5" title="" class="ltx_ref">5</a>]</cite>. These foundational studies demonstrated the prognostic value of serial imaging but relied on handcrafted volumetric endpoints rather than learned representations. Subsequent deep-learning approaches focused on pretreatment imaging: Ha <em id="S2.SS1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">et al.</em> used pretrained CNN features from postcontrast MRI <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib8" title="" class="ltx_ref">8</a>]</cite>, Braman <em id="S2.SS1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">et al.</em> modeled intratumoral and peritumoral DCE-MRI features with multi-institutional validation <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib9" title="" class="ltx_ref">9</a>]</cite>, and Comes <em id="S2.SS1.p1.1.3" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">et al.</em> applied transfer learning to pretreatment scans <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib6" title="" class="ltx_ref">6</a>]</cite>. Multimodal methods further integrated MRI with molecular and demographic variables <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib11" title="" class="ltx_ref">11</a>, <a href="#bib.bib10" title="" class="ltx_ref">10</a>]</cite>, and attention-based architectures fused whole-breast 3-D MRI with clinical features through self-attention <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib7" title="" class="ltx_ref">7</a>]</cite>. BreastDCEDL standardized a large multicenter DCE-MRI resource for systematic comparison <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib23" title="" class="ltx_ref">23</a>]</cite>. Across these studies, clinical and treatment variables are either absent from the model or appended as covariates in the outcome classifier. <span id="S2.SS1.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text">CoRe-WM</span> instead integrates these variables directly into a learned state-transition function, enabling treatment-conditioned dynamics modeling that updates predictions as each new visit arrives.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S2.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection"><span id="S2.SS2.6" class="ltx_text">II-B</span> </span><span id="S2.SS2.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Longitudinal Medical Image Modeling</span></h3>

<div id="S2.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Longitudinal imaging methods span pairwise change models, sequence encoders, and future-state generators. Siamese and multitask networks compare repeated scans for cancer assessment <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib24" title="" class="ltx_ref">24</a>, <a href="#bib.bib25" title="" class="ltx_ref">25</a>]</cite>, while recurrent and attention models aggregate longer imaging histories in neuroimaging and ophthalmology <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib26" title="" class="ltx_ref">26</a>, <a href="#bib.bib27" title="" class="ltx_ref">27</a>, <a href="#bib.bib28" title="" class="ltx_ref">28</a>]</cite>. More recently, Transformers have been applied to cross-timepoint interactions for treatment response prediction <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib29" title="" class="ltx_ref">29</a>]</cite>, and neural ODEs to continuous-time latent disease progression <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib30" title="" class="ltx_ref">30</a>]</cite>. In breast cancer, baseline and on-treatment MRI have been combined through phase concatenation <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib31" title="" class="ltx_ref">31</a>]</cite>, uncertainty-aware prediction <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib14" title="" class="ltx_ref">14</a>]</cite>, multimodal longitudinal fusion <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib15" title="" class="ltx_ref">15</a>]</cite>, and spatiotemporal interaction modeling <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib16" title="" class="ltx_ref">16</a>]</cite>. Huang <em id="S2.SS2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">et al.</em> introduced self-supervised temporal-order pretraining on longitudinal breast MRI with multicenter validation <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib32" title="" class="ltx_ref">32</a>]</cite>. More explicit trajectory methods transfer later latent features to an early predictor <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib33" title="" class="ltx_ref">33</a>]</cite>, regularize four-visit phenotype trajectories with responder-alignment objectives <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib34" title="" class="ltx_ref">34</a>]</cite>, or construct spatiotemporal response graphs from longitudinal imaging <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib35" title="" class="ltx_ref">35</a>]</cite>. These approaches demonstrate that temporal structure carries information beyond baseline imaging. Most, however, optimize the temporal representation directly for the clinical endpoint, coupling the learning of state dynamics with outcome prediction. This design does not separate the representation of imaging-state evolution from the task of predicting pCR, and may require examinations that are unavailable at earlier decision points. <span id="S2.SS2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text">CoRe-WM</span> addresses this by learning from every valid next-visit transition without outcome labels, supporting evaluation at arbitrary observed prefixes, and freezing the trajectory representation before outcome prediction.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S2.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection"><span id="S2.SS3.6" class="ltx_text">II-C</span> </span><span id="S2.SS3.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">World Models and JEPA</span></h3>

<div id="S2.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">World models learn an internal state and dynamics that predict future observations under actions or context. Recurrent visual world models <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib17" title="" class="ltx_ref">17</a>]</cite>, Dreamer <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib18" title="" class="ltx_ref">18</a>]</cite>, and DreamerV3 <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib19" title="" class="ltx_ref">19</a>]</cite> demonstrated this paradigm in reinforcement learning, where generative models predict pixels or observations to support planning. JEPA offers a complementary formulation that predicts target representations instead of raw observations: I-JEPA applies this to masked image regions <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib20" title="" class="ltx_ref">20</a>]</cite>, V-JEPA extends it to video <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib21" title="" class="ltx_ref">21</a>]</cite>, and LeWorldModel studies stable latent prediction with distribution regularization <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib36" title="" class="ltx_ref">36</a>]</cite>. Medical adaptations of these ideas are emerging. CheXWorld applied a world-model objective to chest X-ray representation learning <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib37" title="" class="ltx_ref">37</a>]</cite>. Volumetric JEPA pretraining has been explored for 3-D medical images <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib38" title="" class="ltx_ref">38</a>]</cite>, alongside multimodal image-record prediction <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib39" title="" class="ltx_ref">39</a>]</cite>, generative tumor simulation for treatment planning <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib40" title="" class="ltx_ref">40</a>]</cite>, event-based patient simulation from electronic health records <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib41" title="" class="ltx_ref">41</a>]</cite>, and action-conditioned physiologic forecasting <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib42" title="" class="ltx_ref">42</a>]</cite>. These studies collectively demonstrate the potential of predictive state representations in medicine. <span id="S2.SS3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text">CoRe-WM</span> extends this direction to longitudinal breast DCE-MRI, using assigned therapy and patient biology as observed context, predicting the next-visit latent rather than future pixels, and coupling imaging appearance with a factorized response state that explicitly tracks treatment-induced morphological change.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S3" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">III </span><span id="S3.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Methods</span></h2>

<figure id="S3.F1" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2610.25333v1/Fig1.png" id="S3.F1.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/169;" width="476" height="169" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S3.F1.7" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Fig. 1</span>: </span><span id="S3.F1.8" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Overview of <span id="S3.F1.8.1" class="ltx_text">CoRe-WM</span>. <span id="S3.F1.8.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">(A)</span> Outcome-free pretraining. The upper pathway encodes DCE-MRI visits into latent states and predicts the next latent via a conditioned causal Transformer; the lower pathway operates on lesion geometry descriptors to produce a factorized response state <math id="S3.F1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\mathbf{s}}_{t+1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐬</mi><mo mathsize="1.110em">^</mo></mover><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\mathbf{s}}_{t+1}</annotation></semantics></math>, which corrects the latent prediction and is supervised by the <span id="S3.F1.8.3" class="ltx_text">IRG</span> loss. Patient profile, treatment, and temporal embeddings condition both pathways through FiLM modulation <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib43" title="" class="ltx_ref">43</a>]</cite>. The EMA target encoder <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib44" title="" class="ltx_ref">44</a>]</cite> provides the stable prediction target. <span id="S3.F1.8.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">(B)</span> pCR prediction. All parameters are frozen; accumulated response states at each decision point are passed to a linear readout for progressively updated pCR estimates.</span></figcaption>
</figure>
<section id="S3.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection"><span id="S3.SS1.6" class="ltx_text">III-A</span> </span><span id="S3.SS1.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Problem Formulation</span></h3>

<div id="S3.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We formulate treatment response prediction as a two-stage problem. In the first stage, we learn a conditioned state-transition model that implicitly encodes the patient’s treatment response in a self-supervised manner, without access to outcome labels. In the second stage, the learned state representations are frozen and a linear readout predicts clinical outcome from the accumulated state trajectory (Fig. <a href="#S3.F1" title="Fig. 1 ‣ III Methods ‣ CoRe-WM: Conditioned Response-State World Modeling for Longitudinal Treatment-Response Prediction in Breast DCE-MRI" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>).</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">At each timepoint <math id="S3.SS1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>, we define the patient’s <em id="S3.SS1.p2.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">latent state</em> <math id="S3.SS1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{z}_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐳</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{z}_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> as a joint encoding of the imaging appearance, captured by a volumetric image <math id="S3.SS1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="I_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>I</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">I_{t}</annotation></semantics></math>, and the lesion geometry, summarized by a compact descriptor <math id="S3.SS1.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{q}_{t}\in\mathbb{R}^{D_{q}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝐪</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>q</mi></msub></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{q}_{t}\in\mathbb{R}^{D_{q}}</annotation></semantics></math> (e.g., volume, shape, and position). The state is obtained through a learned encoder <math id="S3.SS1.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{z}_{t}=\text{Enc}_{\theta}(I_{t},\mathbf{q}_{t})\in\mathbb{R}^{D_{z}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝐳</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mtext>Enc</mtext><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>I</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>𝐪</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>z</mi></msub></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{z}_{t}=\text{Enc}_{\theta}(I_{t},\mathbf{q}_{t})\in\mathbb{R}^{D_{z}}</annotation></semantics></math>. The evolution of <math id="S3.SS1.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{z}_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐳</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{z}_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> across timepoints constitutes the patient’s treatment-response trajectory. This trajectory is governed by a <em id="S3.SS1.p2.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">state transition</em> conditioned on the patient’s baseline clinical profile <math id="S3.SS1.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{b}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝐛</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{b}</annotation></semantics></math> (e.g., receptor status) and the administered treatment <math id="S3.SS1.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{a}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝐚</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{a}</annotation></semantics></math> (e.g., drug regimen), denoted collectively as <math id="S3.SS1.p2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{c}=(\mathbf{b},\mathbf{a})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝐜</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐛</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝐚</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{c}=(\mathbf{b},\mathbf{a})</annotation></semantics></math>. The central task is to learn a transition function</p>
<table id="S3.E1" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E1.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\hat{\mathbf{z}}_{t+1}=T_{\theta}(\mathbf{z}_{0:t},\;\mathbf{c})" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐳</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>T</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝐳</mi><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><mo rspace="0.447em">,</mo><mi>𝐜</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\mathbf{z}}_{t+1}=T_{\theta}(\mathbf{z}_{0:t},\;\mathbf{c})</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(1)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS1.p2.2" class="ltx_p">that, given the observed state prefix <math id="S3.SS1.p2.m10" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\mathbf{z}_{0:t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝐳</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{z}_{0:t}</annotation></semantics></math> and the condition <math id="S3.SS1.p2.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{c}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝐜</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{c}</annotation></semantics></math>, predicts the next state <math id="S3.SS1.p2.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\mathbf{z}}_{t+1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐳</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\mathbf{z}}_{t+1}</annotation></semantics></math> in latent space.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">In parallel with the image-level prediction, a factorized response pathway (Section <a href="#S3.SS4" title="III-D Factorized Future Response State ‣ III Methods ‣ CoRe-WM: Conditioned Response-State World Modeling for Longitudinal Treatment-Response Prediction in Breast DCE-MRI" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">III-D</span></a>) processes the lesion geometry sequence <math id="S3.SS1.p3.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\mathbf{q}_{0:t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝐪</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{q}_{0:t}</annotation></semantics></math> under the same condition <math id="S3.SS1.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{c}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝐜</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{c}</annotation></semantics></math> and produces a compact response state <math id="S3.SS1.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\mathbf{s}}_{t+1}\in\mathbb{R}^{D_{s}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐬</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>s</mi></msub></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\mathbf{s}}_{t+1}\in\mathbb{R}^{D_{s}}</annotation></semantics></math> (<math id="S3.SS1.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D_{s}\ll D_{z}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><mo>≪</mo><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>z</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D_{s}\ll D_{z}</annotation></semantics></math>) that captures treatment-response dynamics in a low-dimensional space separate from imaging appearance. Once the transition model is trained, all parameters are frozen. For a patient with <math id="S3.SS1.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>T</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T</annotation></semantics></math> observed visits, a linear readout aggregates the accumulated response states <math id="S3.SS1.p3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\mathbf{s}}_{1},\ldots,\hat{\mathbf{s}}_{T-1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐬</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐬</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\mathbf{s}}_{1},\ldots,\hat{\mathbf{s}}_{T-1}</annotation></semantics></math> and maps them to the binary endpoint <math id="S3.SS1.p3.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="y\in\{0,1\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y\in\{0,1\}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection"><span id="S3.SS2.6" class="ltx_text">III-B</span> </span><span id="S3.SS2.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Latent State Encoder</span></h3>

<div id="S3.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Each visit is characterized by a volumetric image <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="I_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>I</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">I_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> and a compact lesion descriptor <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{q}_{t}\in\mathbb{R}^{D_{q}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝐪</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>q</mi></msub></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{q}_{t}\in\mathbb{R}^{D_{q}}</annotation></semantics></math> that summarizes the geometry of the region of interest within the imaging field. We encode these two modalities separately and combine them additively:</p>
<table id="S3.E2" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{z}_{t}=g_{\theta}\!\bigl(f_{\theta}(I_{t})\bigr)+h_{\theta}(\mathbf{q}_{t})" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝐳</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>f</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>I</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝐪</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{z}_{t}=g_{\theta}\!\bigl(f_{\theta}(I_{t})\bigr)+h_{\theta}(\mathbf{q}_{t})</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(2)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS2.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f_{\theta}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>f</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f_{\theta}</annotation></semantics></math> is a 3-D residual convolutional network that maps the volumetric input to an appearance vector, <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g_{\theta}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g_{\theta}</annotation></semantics></math> is a nonlinear projector, and <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h_{\theta}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h_{\theta}</annotation></semantics></math> is a geometry projector. All three operate in a shared <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D_{z}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>z</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D_{z}</annotation></semantics></math>-dimensional latent space. The appearance encoder progressively downsamples the input volume through multiple residual stages to a single vector, which is then projected into the latent space. The geometry projector maps the low-dimensional descriptor <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{q}_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐪</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{q}_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> into the same space through a lightweight MLP.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The encoder above, referred to as the <em id="S3.SS2.p2.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">online encoder</em>, encodes the observed states that serve as input to the transition function. A second encoder, the <em id="S3.SS2.p2.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">target encoder</em>, provides the prediction targets representing future states. The target encoder shares the same architecture but maintains separate parameters <math id="S3.SS2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\phi" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ϕ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\phi</annotation></semantics></math>, updated as an exponential moving average (EMA) of the online parameters: <math id="S3.SS2.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\phi\leftarrow\mu\,\phi+(1-\mu)\,\theta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ϕ</mi><mo stretchy="false">←</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>μ</mi><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>ϕ</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>μ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>θ</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\phi\leftarrow\mu\,\phi+(1-\mu)\,\theta</annotation></semantics></math> after each gradient step. Its slowly evolving parameters provide a stable prediction objective that prevents degenerate solutions such as representational collapse. This online-target pair forms the basis of the JEPA <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib20" title="" class="ltx_ref">20</a>, <a href="#bib.bib21" title="" class="ltx_ref">21</a>]</cite> framework adopted in our transition function.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection"><span id="S3.SS3.6" class="ltx_text">III-C</span> </span><span id="S3.SS3.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Conditioned State Transition</span></h3>

<div id="S3.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The clinical profile <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{b}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝐛</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{b}</annotation></semantics></math> and treatment <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{a}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝐚</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{a}</annotation></semantics></math> are each encoded through learned embeddings for categorical variables and normalization for continuous variables, then concatenated to form <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{c}\in\mathbb{R}^{D_{c}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝐜</mi><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>c</mi></msub></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{c}\in\mathbb{R}^{D_{c}}</annotation></semantics></math>. Since <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{c}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝐜</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{c}</annotation></semantics></math> is shared across timepoints, we concatenate a learned temporal embedding at each step to yield per-step condition vectors <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{c}_{t}\in\mathbb{R}^{D_{c}+D_{\tau}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝐜</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>c</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>τ</mi></msub></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{c}_{t}\in\mathbb{R}^{D_{c}+D_{\tau}}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Given the observed latent state sequence <math id="S3.SS3.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\mathbf{z}_{0},\ldots,\mathbf{z}_{t})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝐳</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>𝐳</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\mathbf{z}_{0},\ldots,\mathbf{z}_{t})</annotation></semantics></math> and the corresponding condition sequence <math id="S3.SS3.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\mathbf{c}_{0},\ldots,\mathbf{c}_{t})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝐜</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>𝐜</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\mathbf{c}_{0},\ldots,\mathbf{c}_{t})</annotation></semantics></math>, the conditioned state transition estimates the next latent state. We adopt a conditioned causal Transformer as the transition core. The Transformer encoder uses pre-normalization, an upper-triangular causal mask ensuring that the output at position <math id="S3.SS3.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math> attends only to positions <math id="S3.SS3.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0,\ldots,t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0,\ldots,t</annotation></semantics></math>, and learned positional embeddings to encode temporal position. The condition vector <math id="S3.SS3.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{c}_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐜</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{c}_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> enters through two complementary mechanisms:</p>
</div>
<section id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Additive conditioning.</h5>

<div id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">A linear projection maps <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{c}_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐜</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{c}_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D_{z}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>z</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D_{z}</annotation></semantics></math> dimensions and adds it to the input token at each position before the Transformer layers, providing a global context shift.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Feature-wise linear modulation (FiLM).</h5>

<div id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Within each Transformer layer, a learned projection of <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{c}_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐜</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{c}_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> produces per-dimension scale and shift parameters <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\gamma_{t},\beta_{t})\in\mathbb{R}^{D_{z}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>γ</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>β</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>z</mi></msub></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\gamma_{t},\beta_{t})\in\mathbb{R}^{D_{z}}</annotation></semantics></math>, which modulate the layer’s hidden state <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{h}_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐡</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{h}_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> following the FiLM conditioning mechanism <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib43" title="" class="ltx_ref">43</a>]</cite>:</p>
<table id="S3.E3" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{\mathbf{h}}_{t}=\mathbf{h}_{t}\odot\bigl(1+\eta\,\tanh(\gamma_{t})\bigr)+\eta\,\beta_{t}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐡</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>𝐡</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⊙</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>η</mi><mo lspace="0.337em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>tanh</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>γ</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>η</mi><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>β</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tilde{\mathbf{h}}_{t}=\mathbf{h}_{t}\odot\bigl(1+\eta\,\tanh(\gamma_{t})\bigr)+\eta\,\beta_{t}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(3)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\eta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>η</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\eta</annotation></semantics></math> is a fixed scaling factor and <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\odot" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>⊙</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\odot</annotation></semantics></math> denotes element-wise multiplication. The dual conditioning mechanism balances two competing requirements: the transition should be aware of the treatment context, which determines the expected biological response, but should not learn to predict outcomes from clinical features alone. To this end, the FiLM weights and biases are initialized to zero, so conditioning begins as a near-identity transformation and grows in influence only as training progresses, ensuring that the state dynamics remain the primary signal. A prediction head projects the Transformer output to the latent prediction <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\mathbf{z}}^{\text{pred}}_{t+1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐳</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mtext>pred</mtext></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\mathbf{z}}^{\text{pred}}_{t+1}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection"><span id="S3.SS4.6" class="ltx_text">III-D</span> </span><span id="S3.SS4.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Factorized Future Response State</span></h3>

<div id="S3.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">While the conditioned state transition captures the visual evolution, the high dimensionality of volumetric latents (<math id="S3.SS4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D_{z}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>z</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D_{z}</annotation></semantics></math>) mixes appearance, contrast, and geometry information. We introduce a parallel pathway that operates on the compact lesion descriptors <math id="S3.SS4.p1.m2" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\mathbf{q}_{0:t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝐪</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{q}_{0:t}</annotation></semantics></math> and produces a lower-dimensional future response state <math id="S3.SS4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\mathbf{s}}_{t+1}\in\mathbb{R}^{D_{s}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐬</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>s</mi></msub></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\mathbf{s}}_{t+1}\in\mathbb{R}^{D_{s}}</annotation></semantics></math> (<math id="S3.SS4.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D_{s}\ll D_{z}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><mo>≪</mo><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>z</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D_{s}\ll D_{z}</annotation></semantics></math>) that explicitly tracks the treatment-response trajectory. This factorization encodes the structural prior that treatment response manifests primarily in lesion morphology, guiding the learned representation toward treatment-relevant changes and producing a compact representation suitable for downstream linear readout.</p>
</div>
<section id="S3.SS4.SSS1" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection"><span id="S3.SS4.SSS1.6" class="ltx_text">III-D</span>1 </span>Temporal Response Dynamics</h4>

<div id="S3.SS4.SSS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS4.SSS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The observed lesion descriptors are first log-transformed on volume-related features to stabilize scale differences across patients, then projected through a two-layer network to a <math id="S3.SS4.SSS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D_{s}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D_{s}</annotation></semantics></math>-dimensional response embedding. A dedicated conditioned causal Transformer, sharing the same FiLM conditioning architecture as the conditioned state transition but with fewer layers, processes the response sequence. The Transformer output at position <math id="S3.SS4.SSS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math> defines the future response state <math id="S3.SS4.SSS1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\mathbf{s}}_{t+1}\in\mathbb{R}^{D_{s}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐬</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>s</mi></msub></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\mathbf{s}}_{t+1}\in\mathbb{R}^{D_{s}}</annotation></semantics></math>. A linear decoder head maps <math id="S3.SS4.SSS1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\mathbf{s}}_{t+1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐬</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\mathbf{s}}_{t+1}</annotation></semantics></math> back to the descriptor space, producing a geometry estimate <math id="S3.SS4.SSS1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\mathbf{q}}_{t+1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐪</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\mathbf{q}}_{t+1}</annotation></semantics></math>. A separate response head decodes a predicted response vector <math id="S3.SS4.SSS1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\mathbf{r}}_{t+1}\in\mathbb{R}^{D_{r}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐫</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>r</mi></msub></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\mathbf{r}}_{t+1}\in\mathbb{R}^{D_{r}}</annotation></semantics></math> and a scalar response score <math id="S3.SS4.SSS1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\rho}_{t+1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>ρ</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\rho}_{t+1}</annotation></semantics></math> from <math id="S3.SS4.SSS1.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\mathbf{s}}_{t+1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐬</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\mathbf{s}}_{t+1}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS4.SSS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS4.SSS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">These predictions are supervised by an Image-derived Response Guidance (<span id="S3.SS4.SSS1.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text">IRG</span>) loss <math id="S3.SS4.SSS1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}_{\text{IRG}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mtext>IRG</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}_{\text{IRG}}</annotation></semantics></math> constructed entirely from observed imaging, without reference to the clinical outcome <math id="S3.SS4.SSS1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="y" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>y</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y</annotation></semantics></math>. At each transition, two outcome-free targets are extracted: a response vector <math id="S3.SS4.SSS1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{r}_{t+1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐫</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{r}_{t+1}</annotation></semantics></math> that concatenates baseline-relative and previous-visit-relative changes in lesion volume, shape, and enhancement intensity, and a scalar response score <math id="S3.SS4.SSS1.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho_{t+1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>ρ</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho_{t+1}</annotation></semantics></math> that aggregates key response components with treatment-category-level standardization. The loss is</p>
<table id="S3.EGx1" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="S3.Ex1"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S3.Ex1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\mathcal{L}_{\text{IRG}}=\;" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mtext>IRG</mtext></msub><mo rspace="0.558em">=</mo><mphantom></mphantom></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\mathcal{L}_{\text{IRG}}=\;</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S3.Ex1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\ell_{\text{H}}(\hat{\mathbf{q}}_{t+1},\,\mathbf{q}_{t+1})+\ell_{\text{H}}(\hat{\mathbf{r}}_{t+1},\,\mathbf{r}_{t+1})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mtext>H</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐪</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>𝐪</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mtext>H</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐫</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>𝐫</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\ell_{\text{H}}(\hat{\mathbf{q}}_{t+1},\,\mathbf{q}_{t+1})+\ell_{\text{H}}(\hat{\mathbf{r}}_{t+1},\,\mathbf{r}_{t+1})</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
<tbody id="S3.Ex2"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_eqn_cell"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S3.Ex2.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\displaystyle+\lambda_{\text{rank}}\!\!\!\sum_{(i,j):\,\rho_{i}&gt;\rho_{j}}\!\!\max\!\bigl(0,\,m-(\hat{\rho}_{i}-\hat{\rho}_{j})\bigr)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>λ</mi><mtext>rank</mtext></msub><mstyle displaystyle="true"><munder><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi><mo rspace="0.278em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.448em">:</mo><mrow><msub><mi>ρ</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>&gt;</mo><msub><mi>ρ</mi><mi>j</mi></msub></mrow></mrow></munder></mstyle><mpadded style="width:1.808em;" width="1.808em"><mi>max</mi></mpadded><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo rspace="0.337em">,</mo><mi>m</mi><mo>−</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>ρ</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>ρ</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>j</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle+\lambda_{\text{rank}}\!\!\!\sum_{(i,j):\,\rho_{i}&gt;\rho_{j}}\!\!\max\!\bigl(0,\,m-(\hat{\rho}_{i}-\hat{\rho}_{j})\bigr)</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
<tbody id="S3.E4"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_eqn_cell"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S3.E4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle+\lambda_{\text{ctr}}\mathcal{L}_{\text{ctr}}(\hat{\mathbf{s}},\,\mathbf{r})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><msub><mi>λ</mi><mtext>ctr</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mtext>ctr</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐬</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>,</mo><mi>𝐫</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle+\lambda_{\text{ctr}}\mathcal{L}_{\text{ctr}}(\hat{\mathbf{s}},\,\mathbf{r})</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(4)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS4.SSS1.p2.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S3.SS4.SSS1.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell_{\text{H}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mtext>H</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell_{\text{H}}</annotation></semantics></math> denotes smooth-<math id="S3.SS4.SSS1.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>L</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L_{1}</annotation></semantics></math> loss, the third term is a pairwise margin ranking loss that preserves the ordinal structure of response magnitude across patients within each batch, and <math id="S3.SS4.SSS1.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}_{\text{ctr}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mtext>ctr</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}_{\text{ctr}}</annotation></semantics></math> is a contrastive loss that pulls response states of patients with similar imaging changes together in the latent space. The geometry estimate <math id="S3.SS4.SSS1.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\mathbf{q}}_{t+1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐪</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\mathbf{q}}_{t+1}</annotation></semantics></math> also serves as input to the latent correction described below.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS4.SSS2" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection"><span id="S3.SS4.SSS2.6" class="ltx_text">III-D</span>2 </span>Latent Correction</h4>

<div id="S3.SS4.SSS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS4.SSS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The response pathway contributes a learned correction to the conditioned state transition through a latent adapter. The adapter concatenates the future response state <math id="S3.SS4.SSS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\mathbf{s}}_{t+1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐬</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\mathbf{s}}_{t+1}</annotation></semantics></math> with the geometry estimate <math id="S3.SS4.SSS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\mathbf{q}}_{t+1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐪</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\mathbf{q}}_{t+1}</annotation></semantics></math> produced by the response Transformer and projects this to the image latent dimension:</p>
<table id="S3.E5" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta\mathbf{z}^{\text{resp}}_{t+1}=\alpha_{z}\cdot\text{Adapt}\!\bigl([\hat{\mathbf{s}}_{t+1};\,\hat{\mathbf{q}}_{t+1}]\bigr)" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>𝐳</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mtext>resp</mtext></msubsup></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>α</mi><mi>z</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><mpadded style="width:2.493em;" width="2.493em"><mtext>Adapt</mtext></mpadded></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐬</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo rspace="0.337em">;</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐪</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta\mathbf{z}^{\text{resp}}_{t+1}=\alpha_{z}\cdot\text{Adapt}\!\bigl([\hat{\mathbf{s}}_{t+1};\,\hat{\mathbf{q}}_{t+1}]\bigr)</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(5)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS4.SSS2.p1.2" class="ltx_p">with a small scaling factor <math id="S3.SS4.SSS2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha_{z}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>α</mi><mi>z</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha_{z}</annotation></semantics></math> and zero-initialized output weights. This ensures the response correction is negligible at the start of training, preventing the response pathway from interfering with the conditioned state transition before either component has learned useful representations. As training proceeds, the adapter learns to communicate response-state information to the image prediction in a complementary fashion.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS5" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection"><span id="S3.SS5.6" class="ltx_text">III-E</span> </span><span id="S3.SS5.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Joint Prediction and Pretraining Objective</span></h3>

<div id="S3.SS5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The final predicted next-visit latent is the sum of the two pathway outputs:</p>
<table id="S3.E6" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\mathbf{z}}_{t+1}=\hat{\mathbf{z}}^{\text{pred}}_{t+1}+\Delta\mathbf{z}^{\text{resp}}_{t+1}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐳</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐳</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mtext>pred</mtext></msubsup><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>𝐳</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mtext>resp</mtext></msubsup></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\mathbf{z}}_{t+1}=\hat{\mathbf{z}}^{\text{pred}}_{t+1}+\Delta\mathbf{z}^{\text{resp}}_{t+1}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(6)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS5.p1.2" class="ltx_p">and the prediction target is the EMA-encoded visit state:</p>
<table id="S3.E7" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E7.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{z}^{\text{tar}}_{t+1}=g_{\phi}\!\bigl(f_{\phi}(I_{t+1})\bigr)+h_{\phi}(\mathbf{q}_{t+1})." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>𝐳</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mtext>tar</mtext></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>ϕ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>f</mi><mi>ϕ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>I</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>ϕ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝐪</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{z}^{\text{tar}}_{t+1}=g_{\phi}\!\bigl(f_{\phi}(I_{t+1})\bigr)+h_{\phi}(\mathbf{q}_{t+1}).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(7)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS5.p1.3" class="ltx_p">Because the target includes both appearance and geometry, the joint prediction accounts for both modalities. The state transition carries the dominant appearance prediction, and the response-state correction allows the factorized response pathway to refine the forecast when lesion-dynamics information provides complementary evidence.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS5.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS5.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The total pretraining loss is a weighted combination of three groups of terms:</p>
<table id="S3.E8" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E8.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}=\lambda_{\text{pred}}\mathcal{L}_{\text{pred}}+\lambda_{\text{sig}}\mathcal{L}_{\text{SIGReg}}+\mathcal{L}_{\text{IRG}}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>λ</mi><mtext>pred</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mtext>pred</mtext></msub></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><msub><mi>λ</mi><mtext>sig</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mtext>SIGReg</mtext></msub></mrow><mo>+</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mtext>IRG</mtext></msub></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}=\lambda_{\text{pred}}\mathcal{L}_{\text{pred}}+\lambda_{\text{sig}}\mathcal{L}_{\text{SIGReg}}+\mathcal{L}_{\text{IRG}}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(8)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS5.p2.2" class="ltx_p">The primary signal <math id="S3.SS5.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}_{\text{pred}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mtext>pred</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}_{\text{pred}}</annotation></semantics></math> is the layer-normalized mean squared error between predicted and target latents, summed over all <math id="S3.SS5.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T{-}1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T{-}1</annotation></semantics></math> transitions with a decaying weight schedule that emphasizes earlier steps. A distributional regularizer <math id="S3.SS5.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}_{\text{SIGReg}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mtext>SIGReg</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}_{\text{SIGReg}}</annotation></semantics></math> (SIGReg <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib36" title="" class="ltx_ref">36</a>]</cite>) prevents representational collapse by encouraging the latent distribution to remain well-spread.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS5.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS5.p3.1" class="ltx_p">The imaging response guidance <math id="S3.SS5.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}_{\text{IRG}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mtext>IRG</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}_{\text{IRG}}</annotation></semantics></math>, defined in Section <a href="#S3.SS4" title="III-D Factorized Future Response State ‣ III Methods ‣ CoRe-WM: Conditioned Response-State World Modeling for Longitudinal Treatment-Response Prediction in Breast DCE-MRI" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">III-D</span></a>, supervises the factorized response pathway using outcome-free targets derived from inter-visit changes in lesion geometry and imaging intensity.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS6" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection"><span id="S3.SS6.6" class="ltx_text">III-F</span> </span><span id="S3.SS6.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Frozen Linear Readout</span></h3>

<div id="S3.SS6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">After pretraining, all model weights are frozen and outcome labels <math id="S3.SS6.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="y" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>y</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y</annotation></semantics></math> are introduced exclusively at this stage. At each decision point, visits up to timepoint <math id="S3.SS6.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> have been observed.
