The response pathway processes these visits and produces future response states <math id="S3.SS6.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\mathbf{s}}_{1},\ldots,\hat{\mathbf{s}}_{k+1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐬</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐬</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\mathbf{s}}_{1},\ldots,\hat{\mathbf{s}}_{k+1}</annotation></semantics></math>, from which a feature vector is constructed by concatenating summary statistics of the observed prefix (initial state, current state, prefix mean, recent revision, cumulative displacement). A single class-balanced logistic regression is trained on the pooled features from all patients and all decision points to predict <math id="S3.SS6.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="y" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>y</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y</annotation></semantics></math>. As more visits are observed, the readout receives a longer state prefix, allowing the prediction to be progressively refined with additional treatment-response information.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S4" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">IV </span><span id="S4.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Experiments</span></h2>

<section id="S4.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection"><span id="S4.SS1.6" class="ltx_text">IV-A</span> </span><span id="S4.SS1.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Datasets and Evaluation Protocol</span></h3>

<div id="S4.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.SS1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Study cohorts.</span> We used DCE-MRI and clinical data from the I-SPY2 (808 patients, 275 pCR) and I-SPY1 (156 patients, 41 pCR) neoadjuvant breast cancer trials <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib13" title="" class="ltx_ref">13</a>, <a href="#bib.bib22" title="" class="ltx_ref">22</a>]</cite>. Both trials acquired MRI at four treatment timepoints (T0–T3). Prediction was evaluated at T0, T0–T1, and T0–T2; T3 was used only during outcome-free pretraining.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.SS1.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">DCE-MRI preprocessing.</span> Each visit was represented by an eight-channel volume comprising precontrast, early postcontrast, late postcontrast, two subtraction, peak enhancement, washout, and binary lesion-region channels. Phase selection followed the BreastDCEDL adaptive protocol <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib23" title="" class="ltx_ref">23</a>]</cite>. Lesion regions were derived from the released functional-tumor-volume analysis masks; automatic enhancement-based localization was used when a compatible mask was unavailable. All image channels were robustly normalized per visit, and each volume was cropped or padded to <math id="S4.SS1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="32\times 96\times 96" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>32</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>96</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>96</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">32\times 96\times 96</annotation></semantics></math> voxels centered on the T0 lesion. A nine-dimensional geometry descriptor was extracted from each ROI mask.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS1.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.SS1.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Five-fold evaluation.</span> Five disjoint patient-level folds were created, stratified by pCR status and HR/HER2 subtype. In each fold, approximately 525 I-SPY2 patients were used for training, 121 for validation, and 162 for testing; the same fold manifest was used for all methods. Reported metrics are fold mean <math id="S4.SS1.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pm" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>±</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pm</annotation></semantics></math> standard deviation, quantifying partition variability. Within each fold, the four non-test partitions were split into training and validation sets; hyperparameters, checkpoints, and classification thresholds were selected on the validation set.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS1.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS1.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.SS1.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Cross-cohort transfer.</span> Each source-fold model, pCR readout, and operating threshold was fitted using I-SPY2 only, and its probability was computed for every I-SPY1 patient. The five source-fold probabilities were averaged for each patient, and the mean source-validation threshold was applied without using I-SPY1 outcomes.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS1.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS1.p5.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.SS1.p5.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Ethics statement.</span> Both I-SPY1 and I-SPY2 are multi-center clinical trials approved by the institutional review boards at each participating site; all participants provided written informed consent prior to enrollment. The imaging and clinical data used in this study were obtained from publicly available, de-identified repositories <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib22" title="" class="ltx_ref">22</a>, <a href="#bib.bib13" title="" class="ltx_ref">13</a>]</cite>. No additional ethics approval was required for this secondary analysis of de-identified data.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection"><span id="S4.SS2.6" class="ltx_text">IV-B</span> </span><span id="S4.SS2.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Implementation Details</span></h3>

<div id="S4.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.SS2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Network configuration.</span> The 3-D encoder used four residual stages (16, 32, 64, 128 channels), producing a 192-dimensional visit representation via global pooling and layer normalization. The transition predictor had three Transformer blocks (4 heads, 512-dim feed-forward, dropout 0.1) conditioned on a 25-dimensional vector encoding visit position, treatment, molecular profile, and age. The factorized response branch mapped the nine-dimensional lesion descriptor to a 64-dimensional response state.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.SS2.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Optimization.</span> Models were trained with AdamW (lr <math id="S4.SS2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="5\times 10^{-5}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>5</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">5\times 10^{-5}</annotation></semantics></math>, weight decay <math id="S4.SS2.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="10^{-4}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10^{-4}</annotation></semantics></math>, batch size 32) for at most 100 epochs with early stopping (patience 4). The target encoder used EMA momentum 0.996. Future-transition losses for T1, T2, and T3 were weighted 2, 1, and 0.5. Loss weights were <math id="S4.SS2.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda_{\text{pred}}=1.0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>λ</mi><mtext>pred</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1.0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda_{\text{pred}}=1.0</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S4.SS2.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda_{\text{sig}}=0.09" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>λ</mi><mtext>sig</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0.09</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda_{\text{sig}}=0.09</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S4.SS2.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda_{\text{rank}}=1.0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>λ</mi><mtext>rank</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1.0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda_{\text{rank}}=1.0</annotation></semantics></math> (margin <math id="S4.SS2.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m=0.1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m=0.1</annotation></semantics></math>), <math id="S4.SS2.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda_{\text{ctr}}=0.02" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>λ</mi><mtext>ctr</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0.02</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda_{\text{ctr}}=0.02</annotation></semantics></math>. The FiLM scaling factor was <math id="S4.SS2.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\eta=0.1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>η</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\eta=0.1</annotation></semantics></math>, and the response adapter scaling factor was <math id="S4.SS2.p2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha_{z}=0.05" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>α</mi><mi>z</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0.05</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha_{z}=0.05</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS2.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS2.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.SS2.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Readout and metrics.</span> After pretraining, all parameters were frozen and a class-balanced logistic readout was fitted on frozen response states; penalty type and regularization strength were selected on the validation fold. AUROC was the primary metric; thresholds were selected by maximizing Youden’s index on validation data. Confidence intervals used patient-level bootstrap of pooled out-of-fold predictions.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection"><span id="S4.SS3.6" class="ltx_text">IV-C</span> </span><span id="S4.SS3.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Comparison with Other Methods</span></h3>

<section id="S4.SS3.SSS1" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection"><span id="S4.SS3.SSS1.6" class="ltx_text">IV-C</span>1 </span>Compared Methods</h4>

<div id="S4.SS3.SSS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS3.SSS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We compared <span id="S4.SS3.SSS1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text">CoRe-WM</span> with published methods and matched baselines under the same five folds. For pretreatment methods, <span id="S4.SS3.SSS1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">ViT</span> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib23" title="" class="ltx_ref">23</a>]</cite> used the BreastDCEDL MinCrop representation with a ViT-B/16 initialized from ImageNet masked-autoencoder weights, evaluated both as a standalone image encoder and with its full two-stage clinical–geometry fusion pipeline. <span id="S4.SS3.SSS1.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">3-D ResNet</span> was a matched pretreatment baseline that encoded the T0 eight-channel volume with the same four-stage 3-D residual network (16, 32, 64, 128 channels) used in <span id="S4.SS3.SSS1.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text">CoRe-WM</span> and mapped its globally pooled representation directly to pCR. For longitudinal methods, <span id="S4.SS3.SSS1.p1.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">PrefixGRU</span> was a matched sequential baseline that applied a shared 3-D encoder to each available visit and aggregated the ordered visit representations with a GRU before pCR classification. <span id="S4.SS3.SSS1.p1.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Temporal representation learning</span> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib34" title="" class="ltx_ref">34</a>]</cite> used MIP-based inputs with reconstruction, temporal-continuity, and responder-alignment objectives. The <span id="S4.SS3.SSS1.p1.1.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">two-stage dual-task</span> model of Jing and Wang <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib33" title="" class="ltx_ref">33</a>]</cite> jointly optimized pCR prediction and future-latent prediction from three-channel early-subtraction inputs with clinical variables. <span id="S4.SS3.SSS1.p1.1.8" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">BSTNet</span> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib32" title="" class="ltx_ref">32</a>]</cite> used temporal-order pretraining on peak-postcontrast volumes from all four visits; the pretrained encoder was retained and a lightweight pCR head was retrained to accept T0–T2 prefixes. Reimplementations followed released architectures when code was available and were selected without test-fold data.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS3.SSS2" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection"><span id="S4.SS3.SSS2.6" class="ltx_text">IV-C</span>2 </span>Results</h4>

<figure id="S4.T1" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table"><span id="S4.T1.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">TABLE I</span>: </span><span id="S4.T1.5" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Five-fold I-SPY2 comparison using the same patient splits and seed for all methods. Values are fold mean <math id="S4.T1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pm" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>±</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pm</annotation></semantics></math> standard deviation. The “Available MRI” column lists the examinations used by the pCR predictor; T3 may additionally be used as an outcome-free pretraining target (<span id="S4.T1.5.1" class="ltx_text">CoRe-WM</span> and BSTNet temporal-order pretraining). ViT two-stage fusion uses the complete BreastDCEDL clinical and geometry feature set. Accuracy, sensitivity, and specificity use a validation-selected threshold.</span></figcaption>

<td id="S4.T1.6.4.8" class="ltx_td ltx_nopad_r ltx_align_center" style="padding:0.3pt 4.0pt;"><math id="S4.T1.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.4022\pm 0.1661" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn mathsize="0.700em">0.4022</mn><mo mathsize="0.700em">±</mo><mn mathsize="0.700em">0.1661</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.4022\pm 0.1661</annotation></semantics></math></td></tr>
<tr id="S4.T1.6.5" class="ltx_tr">
<th id="S4.T1.6.5.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_align_top ltx_th ltx_th_row ltx_border_t" style="padding:0.3pt 4.0pt;">
<span id="S4.T1.6.5.1.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_align_top" style="width:34.1pt;">
<span id="S4.T1.6.5.1.1.1" class="ltx_p">
<span id="S4.T1.6.5.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_inline-block">
<span id="S4.T1.6.5.1.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_p"><em id="S4.T1.6.5.1.1.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic" style="font-size:70%;">Longitudinal</em></span>
<span id="S4.T1.6.5.1.1.1.1.2" class="ltx_p"><em id="S4.T1.6.5.1.1.1.1.2.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic" style="font-size:70%;">methods</em></span>

<td id="S4.T1.6.11.6" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb" style="padding:0.3pt 4.0pt;"><math id="S4.T1.m50" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.7141\pm 0.0381" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn mathsize="0.700em">0.7141</mn><mo mathsize="0.700em">±</mo><mn mathsize="0.700em">0.0381</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.7141\pm 0.0381</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td id="S4.T1.6.11.7" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb" style="padding:0.3pt 4.0pt;"><math id="S4.T1.m51" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.6436\pm 0.1224" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn mathsize="0.700em">0.6436</mn><mo mathsize="0.700em">±</mo><mn mathsize="0.700em">0.1224</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.6436\pm 0.1224</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td id="S4.T1.6.11.8" class="ltx_td ltx_nopad_r ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb" style="padding:0.3pt 4.0pt;"><math id="S4.T1.m52" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.7504\pm 0.1116" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn mathsize="0.700em">0.7504</mn><mo mathsize="0.700em">±</mo><mn mathsize="0.700em">0.1116</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.7504\pm 0.1116</annotation></semantics></math></td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
</figure>
<div id="S4.SS3.SSS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS3.SSS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Table <a href="#S4.T1" title="TABLE I ‣ IV-C2 Results ‣ IV-C Comparison with Other Methods ‣ IV Experiments ‣ CoRe-WM: Conditioned Response-State World Modeling for Longitudinal Treatment-Response Prediction in Breast DCE-MRI" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">I</span></a> shows that <span id="S4.SS3.SSS2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text">CoRe-WM</span> produced the strongest discrimination at every prospective decision point. At T0, its AUROC of <math id="S4.SS3.SSS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.7337\pm 0.0320" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>0.7337</mn><mo>±</mo><mn>0.0320</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.7337\pm 0.0320</annotation></semantics></math> exceeded the ViT (<math id="S4.SS3.SSS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.5591\pm 0.0320" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>0.5591</mn><mo>±</mo><mn>0.0320</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.5591\pm 0.0320</annotation></semantics></math>), the two-stage fusion model (<math id="S4.SS3.SSS2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.5950\pm 0.0130" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>0.5950</mn><mo>±</mo><mn>0.0130</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.5950\pm 0.0130</annotation></semantics></math>), and the matched 3-D ResNet (<math id="S4.SS3.SSS2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.5444\pm 0.0391" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>0.5444</mn><mo>±</mo><mn>0.0391</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.5444\pm 0.0391</annotation></semantics></math>). Once T1 became available, <span id="S4.SS3.SSS2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text">CoRe-WM</span> reached <math id="S4.SS3.SSS2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.7545\pm 0.0468" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>0.7545</mn><mo>±</mo><mn>0.0468</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.7545\pm 0.0468</annotation></semantics></math>, compared with <math id="S4.SS3.SSS2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.6958\pm 0.0193" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>0.6958</mn><mo>±</mo><mn>0.0193</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.6958\pm 0.0193</annotation></semantics></math> for the two-stage dual-task model. In pooled out-of-fold predictions, the AUROC difference between these two methods at T0–T1 was 0.0673 (95% CI, 0.0344–0.0995; <math id="S4.SS3.SSS2.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p=0.0004" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.0004</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p=0.0004</annotation></semantics></math>). The proposed model improved further to <math id="S4.SS3.SSS2.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.7620\pm 0.0363" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>0.7620</mn><mo>±</mo><mn>0.0363</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.7620\pm 0.0363</annotation></semantics></math> with T2, whereas PrefixGRU (<math id="S4.SS3.SSS2.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.5784\pm 0.0668" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>0.5784</mn><mo>±</mo><mn>0.0668</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.5784\pm 0.0668</annotation></semantics></math>), temporal representation learning (<math id="S4.SS3.SSS2.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.5179\pm 0.0516" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>0.5179</mn><mo>±</mo><mn>0.0516</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.5179\pm 0.0516</annotation></semantics></math>), and BSTNet (<math id="S4.SS3.SSS2.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.6578\pm 0.0555" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>0.6578</mn><mo>±</mo><mn>0.0555</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.6578\pm 0.0555</annotation></semantics></math>) all remained substantially lower at the same T0–T2 decision point.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS3.SSS2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS3.SSS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The trajectory results also distinguish the contribution of newly observed response from baseline prognostic information. The mean AUROC increased by 0.0208 from T0 to T0–T1 and by a further 0.0075 from T0–T1 to T0–T2, while specificity rose from 0.6325 to 0.7504. The conditioned trajectory adds discriminative information beyond pretreatment phenotype while supporting sequential prediction from a common frozen state.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>

</figure>
<div id="S4.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We examine cross-cohort robustness in I-SPY1 and Table <a href="#S4.T2" title="TABLE II ‣ IV-D Cross-Cohort Transfer to I-SPY1 ‣ IV Experiments ‣ CoRe-WM: Conditioned Response-State World Modeling for Longitudinal Treatment-Response Prediction in Breast DCE-MRI" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">II</span></a> shows substantial variation in transfer performance. The two-stage dual-task model achieved the highest early-treatment AUROC at 0.7635, while <span id="S4.SS4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text">CoRe-WM</span> achieved 0.7396 at T0 and 0.7321 at T0–T1. The paired AUROC difference between <span id="S4.SS4.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text">CoRe-WM</span> and the two-stage dual-task model at T0–T1 was <math id="S4.SS4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-0.0314" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>0.0314</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-0.0314</annotation></semantics></math> (95% CI, <math id="S4.SS4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-0.1274" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>0.1274</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-0.1274</annotation></semantics></math>–0.0606; <math id="S4.SS4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p=0.5167" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.5167</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p=0.5167</annotation></semantics></math>). The 3-D ResNet reached 0.6738 at T0, PrefixGRU reached 0.6494 at T0–T2, and BSTNet reached 0.4390 at T0–T2. Temporal representation learning reached 0.5548 at T0–T2. At T0, <span id="S4.SS4.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text">CoRe-WM</span> exceeded the ViT, its two-stage fusion, and temporal representation learning by 0.1812, 0.1646, and 0.1922 AUROC, respectively (<math id="S4.SS4.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p=0.0080" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.0080</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p=0.0080</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S4.SS4.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p=0.0124" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.0124</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p=0.0124</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S4.SS4.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p=0.0008" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.0008</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p=0.0008</annotation></semantics></math>). These results indicate that temporal capacity alone did not ensure robustness across trial cohorts. Unlike its I-SPY2 trajectory, <span id="S4.SS4.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text">CoRe-WM</span> did not improve as later I-SPY1 examinations were added: AUROC decreased from 0.7396 at T0 to 0.7321 at T0–T1 and 0.7082 at T0–T2. The transferred operating points were imbalanced for the two-stage dual-task model (high specificity, low sensitivity), and BSTNet fell to near-chance AUROC (0.4390), indicating that its temporal-order pretraining did not confer cross-cohort robustness. These results support cross-cohort feasibility and robustness of <span id="S4.SS4.p1.1.5" class="ltx_text">CoRe-WM</span>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS5" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection"><span id="S4.SS5.6" class="ltx_text">IV-E</span> </span><span id="S4.SS5.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Ablation Study</span></h3>

<div id="S4.SS5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We evaluated the proposed components through a cumulative ablation in which modules were added one at a time to an image-only JEPA. Every configuration used the same five I-SPY2 folds, seed, pretraining budget, and frozen-readout protocol, and was evaluated at the early-treatment T0–T1 decision point. Table <a href="#S4.T3" title="TABLE III ‣ IV-E Ablation Study ‣ IV Experiments ‣ CoRe-WM: Conditioned Response-State World Modeling for Longitudinal Treatment-Response Prediction in Breast DCE-MRI" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">III</span></a> reports model-native fold metrics; the AUROC increment in each row is measured relative to the immediately preceding configuration.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S4.T3" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table"><span id="S4.T3.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">TABLE III</span>: </span><span id="S4.T3.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Cumulative five-fold ablation at T0–T1. Values are fold mean <math id="S4.T3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pm" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>±</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pm</annotation></semantics></math> standard deviation. <math id="S4.T3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta</annotation></semantics></math> AUROC is relative to the preceding row. Patient profile includes HR, HER2, MammaPrint, and age; Tx denotes treatment conditioning; Geo denotes ROI geometry. FRS and IRG denote factorized response state and image-derived response guidance, respectively.</span></figcaption>

<span id="S4.T3.5.7.1.1.1" class="ltx_p ltx_align_left"><math id="S4.T3.m28" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo mathsize="0.700em">+</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S4.T3.5.7.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:70%;"> image-derived response guidance (</span><span id="S4.T3.5.7.1.1.1.2" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:70%;">CoRe-WM</span><span id="S4.T3.5.7.1.1.1.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:70%;">)</span></span>
</span></td>
<td id="S4.T3.5.7.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb" style="padding:0.3pt 2.3pt;"><math id="S4.T3.m29" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\checkmark" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathsize="0.700em">✓</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\checkmark</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td id="S4.T3.5.7.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb" style="padding:0.3pt 2.3pt;"><math id="S4.T3.m30" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\checkmark" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathsize="0.700em">✓</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\checkmark</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td id="S4.T3.5.7.4" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb" style="padding:0.3pt 2.3pt;"><math id="S4.T3.m31" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\checkmark" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathsize="0.700em">✓</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\checkmark</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td id="S4.T3.5.7.5" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb" style="padding:0.3pt 2.3pt;"><span id="S4.T3.5.7.5.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:70%;">FRS+IRG</span></td>
<td id="S4.T3.5.7.6" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb" style="padding:0.3pt 2.3pt;"><math id="S4.T3.m32" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{0.7545\pm 0.0468}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn class="ltx_mathvariant_bold" mathsize="0.700em" mathvariant="bold">0.7545</mn><mo mathsize="0.700em">±</mo><mn class="ltx_mathvariant_bold" mathsize="0.700em" mathvariant="bold">0.0468</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{0.7545\pm 0.0468}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td id="S4.T3.5.7.7" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb" style="padding:0.3pt 2.3pt;"><math id="S4.T3.m33" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+0.0039\pm 0.0082" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo mathsize="0.700em">+</mo><mn mathsize="0.700em">0.0039</mn></mrow><mo mathsize="0.700em">±</mo><mn mathsize="0.700em">0.0082</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+0.0039\pm 0.0082</annotation></semantics></math></td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
</figure>
<div id="S4.SS5.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS5.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The largest gain came from conditioning the image trajectory on patient profile, which increased mean AUROC from 0.5816 to 0.7135. Treatment conditioning did not provide an additional marginal AUROC gain after the clinical variables were introduced, although it remained part of the transition formulation because treatment specifies the context under which the next state is predicted. Adding explicit ROI geometry increased mean AUROC to 0.7380; in pooled out-of-fold predictions, its gain was 0.0253 (95% CI, 0.0001–0.0507). The factorized response state and image-derived response guidance further increased mean AUROC to 0.7506 and 0.7545, respectively. Overall, the ablation indicates that patient profile provides the dominant conditioning signal, while explicit lesion geometry and imaging-derived response guidance contribute smaller but complementary improvements beyond the image-only trajectory.</p>
</div>

</section>
<section id="S4.SS6" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection"><span id="S4.SS6.6" class="ltx_text">IV-F</span> </span><span id="S4.SS6.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Calibration and Decision-Curve Analysis</span></h3>

<div id="S4.SS6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Discrimination alone does not establish whether the predicted probabilities are reliable enough for threshold-based use. We therefore evaluated calibration and decision-curve utility from the five held-out I-SPY2 partitions. Within each outer fold, a Platt calibrator was fitted using that fold’s validation patients and applied without refitting to its test patients. Concatenating the five test partitions yielded one out-of-fold (OOF) probability for each of the 808 I-SPY2 patients. The resulting pooled OOF AUROC is a different estimand from the arithmetic fold-mean AUROC in Table <a href="#S4.T1" title="TABLE I ‣ IV-C2 Results ‣ IV-C Comparison with Other Methods ‣ IV Experiments ‣ CoRe-WM: Conditioned Response-State World Modeling for Longitudinal Treatment-Response Prediction in Breast DCE-MRI" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">I</span></a>; in particular, fold-specific calibration can change rankings between patients belonging to different folds while preserving rankings within each fold.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS6.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS6.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The T0–T2 model had the strongest overall probability performance, with pooled OOF AUROC 0.7288, AUPRC 0.5853, and a calibrated Brier score of 0.1911 (95% CI, 0.1780–0.2045), compared with calibrated Brier scores of 0.1942 at T0 and 0.1949 at T0–T1. Calibration at T0–T2 was close to the ideal line, with intercept <math id="S4.SS6.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-0.020" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>0.020</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-0.020</annotation></semantics></math>, slope 0.978, and expected calibration error 0.0176; Platt scaling reduced its Brier score from 0.2166 before calibration (Fig. <a href="#S4.F2.sf1" title="In Fig. 2 ‣ IV-E Ablation Study ‣ IV Experiments ‣ CoRe-WM: Conditioned Response-State World Modeling for Longitudinal Treatment-Response Prediction in Breast DCE-MRI" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2(a)</span></a>). These findings indicate that the probabilities were well aligned with observed pCR frequency after validation-only recalibration, while the improvement over the earlier decision points was modest.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS6.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS6.p3.1" class="ltx_p">For decision-curve analysis <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib45" title="" class="ltx_ref">45</a>]</cite>, non-pCR was defined as the actionable event and referral for treatment-adaptation review as the modeled action. At T0–T2, the <span id="S4.SS6.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text">CoRe-WM</span> curve exceeded both review-all and review-none strategies across probability thresholds from 0.22 to 0.75 (Fig. <a href="#S4.F2.sf2" title="In Fig. 2 ‣ IV-E Ablation Study ‣ IV Experiments ‣ CoRe-WM: Conditioned Response-State World Modeling for Longitudinal Treatment-Response Prediction in Breast DCE-MRI" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2(b)</span></a>). This range suggests potential utility when the cost of unnecessary review is traded against the cost of missing a patient unlikely to achieve pCR. However, confidence bands overlapped across decision points, and decision-curve net benefit is calculated from predictive outcomes rather than observed effects of changing therapy. We therefore treat this result as exploratory evidence of threshold-dependent utility, not evidence that model-guided treatment adaptation improves patient outcomes.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS7" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection"><span id="S4.SS7.6" class="ltx_text">IV-G</span> </span><span id="S4.SS7.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Receptor-Subtype Stratification</span></h3>

<div id="S4.SS7.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS7.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Table <a href="#S4.T4" title="TABLE IV ‣ IV-G Receptor-Subtype Stratification ‣ IV Experiments ‣ CoRe-WM: Conditioned Response-State World Modeling for Longitudinal Treatment-Response Prediction in Breast DCE-MRI" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">IV</span></a> stratifies the five-fold OOF predictions of <span id="S4.SS7.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text">CoRe-WM</span> by receptor subtype. At T0–T2, the largest pairwise AUROC difference across subtypes was 0.026, and all pairwise confidence intervals crossed zero, indicating that the overall discrimination was not driven by a single subtype. The overall AUROC of 0.762 exceeded each within-subtype value, reflecting the contribution of cross-subtype differences in baseline pCR prevalence to the aggregate discrimination. Among subtypes, TNBC exhibited the largest longitudinal gain from T0 to T0–T2 (<math id="S4.SS7.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+0.067" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>0.067</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+0.067</annotation></semantics></math>; 95% CI, 0.010–0.124); this estimate was not corrected for multiple comparisons and is reported as exploratory.</p>

</section>
<section id="S4.SS8" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection"><span id="S4.SS8.6" class="ltx_text">IV-H</span> </span><span id="S4.SS8.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Condition Dependence and Response-State Grounding</span></h3>

<div id="S4.SS8.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS8.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We examined whether the frozen response state used the clinical and treatment conditions supplied to the transition model. For every outer fold, the fold-specific <span id="S4.SS8.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text">CoRe-WM</span> checkpoint and validation-selected native response-state <span id="S4.SS8.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text">FLR</span> were retained while the held-out MRI latents and lesion geometry were fixed. Treatment was permuted within HR/HER2 strata, clinical profile was permuted within treatment families, and the joint clinical-treatment context was permuted globally. Each scenario used 100 permutations per fold. This design changes only the conditioning pathway and therefore tests whether context contributes to the organization of the learned state.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS8.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS8.p2.1" class="ltx_p">At the primary T0–T2 decision point, the observed-context response state achieved <math id="S4.SS8.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.7621\pm 0.0365" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>0.7621</mn><mo>±</mo><mn>0.0365</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.7621\pm 0.0365</annotation></semantics></math> AUROC. Permuting treatment within biological strata reduced AUROC to <math id="S4.SS8.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.7329\pm 0.0321" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>0.7329</mn><mo>±</mo><mn>0.0321</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.7329\pm 0.0321</annotation></semantics></math>, a mean reduction of <math id="S4.SS8.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.0292\pm 0.0086" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>0.0292</mn><mo>±</mo><mn>0.0086</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.0292\pm 0.0086</annotation></semantics></math>. Permuting clinical profile within treatment family produced a larger reduction to <math id="S4.SS8.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.6476\pm 0.0210" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>0.6476</mn><mo>±</mo><mn>0.0210</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.6476\pm 0.0210</annotation></semantics></math>, and jointly permuting clinical and treatment context reduced AUROC to <math id="S4.SS8.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.5951\pm 0.0242" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>0.5951</mn><mo>±</mo><mn>0.0242</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.5951\pm 0.0242</annotation></semantics></math> (Fig. <a href="#S4.F2.sf3" title="In Fig. 2 ‣ IV-E Ablation Study ‣ IV Experiments ‣ CoRe-WM: Conditioned Response-State World Modeling for Longitudinal Treatment-Response Prediction in Breast DCE-MRI" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2(c)</span></a>). Every perturbation reduced AUROC in all five folds. The larger effect of clinical-profile permutation is consistent with the cumulative ablation, in which molecular profile and age supplied the largest conditioning gain. The smaller treatment-permutation effect should be interpreted in the context of limited treatment-subtype overlap. These perturbations establish model dependence on the observed conditions, but they neither identify causal treatment effects nor estimate outcomes under unassigned regimens.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS8.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS8.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Finally, we tested whether the cumulative response-state update retained an observable measure of treatment response. Within each fold, an outcome-free ridge probe mapped the frozen T0-to-T2 state change to log-volume shrinkage, <math id="S4.SS8.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\log(V_{\mathrm{T0}}/V_{\mathrm{T2}})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>V</mi><mi>T0</mi></msub><mo>/</mo><msub><mi>V</mi><mi>T2</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\log(V_{\mathrm{T0}}/V_{\mathrm{T2}})</annotation></semantics></math>. Its regularization strength was selected using the corresponding validation partition, and prediction was restricted to the held-out partition. Across 791 OOF patients, predicted and observed shrinkage had Spearman correlation 0.8623 (95% CI, 0.8347–0.8865), fold-mean correlation <math id="S4.SS8.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.8608\pm 0.0500" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>0.8608</mn><mo>±</mo><mn>0.0500</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.8608\pm 0.0500</annotation></semantics></math>, and pooled <math id="S4.SS8.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R^{2}=0.6744" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>R</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>0.6744</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R^{2}=0.6744</annotation></semantics></math> (Fig. <a href="#S4.F2.sf4" title="In Fig. 2 ‣ IV-E Ablation Study ‣ IV Experiments ‣ CoRe-WM: Conditioned Response-State World Modeling for Longitudinal Treatment-Response Prediction in Breast DCE-MRI" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2(d)</span></a>). Median observed shrinkage was 1.9005 among non-pCR patients and 2.7631 among pCR patients (<math id="S4.SS8.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p=7.03\times 10^{-15}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>7.03</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>15</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p=7.03\times 10^{-15}</annotation></semantics></math>, descriptive Mann–Whitney test). Because lesion-volume change contributes to the imaging-derived response guidance used during pretraining, this analysis verifies that the intended geometric response signal is retained and generalizes to held-out patients; it does not represent independent discovery of an unsupervised volume biomarker.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S5" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">V </span><span id="S5.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Discussion</span></h2>

<div id="S5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The cumulative ablation shows that patient profile contributes the largest performance gain (image-only JEPA 0.5816 <math id="S5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\to" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\to</annotation></semantics></math> 0.7135). This result is consistent with the well-established association between receptor subtype and pCR rates <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib1" title="" class="ltx_ref">1</a>, <a href="#bib.bib12" title="" class="ltx_ref">12</a>]</cite>: pCR exceeds 40% in HER2-positive and triple-negative tumors while remaining below 20% in HR-positive/HER2-negative disease. Knowing the patient’s receptor status and associated clinical characteristics therefore provides a strong baseline for pCR discrimination, and the conditioning mechanism allows this prior to shape the learned state trajectory from the outset. The condition-permutation analysis (Fig. <a href="#S4.F2.sf3" title="In Fig. 2 ‣ IV-E Ablation Study ‣ IV Experiments ‣ CoRe-WM: Conditioned Response-State World Modeling for Longitudinal Treatment-Response Prediction in Breast DCE-MRI" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2(c)</span></a>) further confirms this role: permuting clinical profile within treatment families reduced five-fold AUROC from 0.7621 to 0.6476 at T0–T2, and jointly permuting clinical and treatment context reduced it to 0.5951, with every perturbation reducing AUROC in all five folds.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Treatment conditioning yielded no additional marginal AUROC increment in the ablation (<math id="S5.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-0.0019" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>0.0019</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-0.0019</annotation></semantics></math>), yet the condition-permutation analysis shows that the transition model does encode treatment information in the frozen response state. Permuting treatment within biological strata reduced T0–T2 AUROC by <math id="S5.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.0292\pm 0.0086" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>0.0292</mn><mo>±</mo><mn>0.0086</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.0292\pm 0.0086</annotation></semantics></math> across all five folds (Fig. <a href="#S4.F2.sf3" title="In Fig. 2 ‣ IV-E Ablation Study ‣ IV Experiments ‣ CoRe-WM: Conditioned Response-State World Modeling for Longitudinal Treatment-Response Prediction in Breast DCE-MRI" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2(c)</span></a>). The contrast between the ablation and permutation results reflects the strong correlation between treatment assignment and receptor subtype in I-SPY2, where biological subtype largely determines treatment-arm eligibility. Treatment conditioning therefore serves a representational role, specifying the context under which the next state is predicted, rather than acting as an independent source of pCR discrimination in this cohort.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Limitations.</span> The image-only JEPA baseline achieved an AUROC of only 0.5816 at T0–T1, and the matched 3-D ResNet and PrefixGRU baselines similarly remained below 0.60 at most decision points. These results indicate that learning discriminative imaging features from the available sample size remains challenging for all evaluated architectures. The explicit geometry pathway and response guidance partially compensate for this by encoding structural priors about lesion morphology, but the reliance on handcrafted geometry descriptors limits the model’s capacity to discover novel imaging biomarkers. Improving image-only representation learning under limited longitudinal data is an important direction for future work. Although cross-cohort transfer to I-SPY1 provides preliminary evidence of generalization, independent external validation on larger and more diverse cohorts remains necessary and is currently limited by the availability of longitudinal DCE-MRI datasets with matched clinical data and annotations.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S6" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">VI </span><span id="S6.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Conclusion</span></h2>

<div id="S6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We presented <span id="S6.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text">CoRe-WM</span>, a world-model framework that formulates longitudinal pCR prediction as conditioned next-state prediction rather than direct outcome classification. The model learns a state-transition function from serial DCE-MRI, assigned therapy, and patient clinical profile, producing frozen response states that are linearly probed for pCR prediction at each decision point. Our experiments establish world-model-based representation learning as a promising framework for outcome prediction in oncology and beyond.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="Sx1" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section">Data and Code Availability</h2>

<div id="Sx1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Sx1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">I-SPY1 and I-SPY2 are de-identified public collections distributed by TCIA <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib22" title="" class="ltx_ref">22</a>, <a href="#bib.bib13" title="" class="ltx_ref">13</a>]</cite>. Code for preprocessing, training, evaluation, and figure generation will be made publicly available upon publication.</p>
</div>
</section>
